newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond spreads narrow, MobileMedia drops.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond spreads narrow, MobileMedia drops.

text.p: Continued strong demand pushed high-grade U.S. corporate bond spreads in for a second session while an earnings warning from MobileMedia sent $460 million in junk-rated notes lower, dealers said.
Investors vying for yield lifted bids for both high-grade and junk bonds as Treasuries closed lower, dealers said.

High-grade spreads narrowed three basis points across most sectors, traders said, with brisk activity surrounding a still thin new issue sector. Higher yielding investment grade bonds garnered most interest, with A-rated bonds tighter by one to two basis points, traders added.
In company-specific trade, an earnings warning from MobileMedia Corp sent its 9-3/8 percent notes down four points, one high-yield trader said.
The debt closed at 86 bid, 87 offer. MobileMedia Corp zero coupon notes due 2003 fell five points to a 70 bid, 74 offer.
Trade in MobileMedia shares was temporarily halted on the NASDAQ before 1200 EDT and the shares closed off two at 4-1/2.
The company said earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization for the third quarter ending September 30 are expected to be about $35 million.
It also warned the third quarter results could put it in violation of bank credit covenants.

Friday's new issuance was topped by $500 million A1/A-plus rated notes due 2008 from Ford Motor Co. The notes were priced to yield 7.306 percent, or 69 basis points over the 10-year Treasury via Lehman Brothers.
Traders noted the issue prompted hedges in the Treasury market, sapping some price gains there.
Thursday's News America Holdings Inc $240 million 30-year deal with a 10-year put closed at a 76 bid, just inside the original spread of 78 basis points.
Coca-Cola Enterprises' $300 million 30-year debt traded at a tight 32 basis point spread compared to Wednesday's issue spread of 33 basis points.
Turning to high-yielders, traders said prices made marginal gains in spots. Some new issues, up more than two points on the break, either held gains or were quoted higher.
Muzak priced $100 million seven-year senior notes at par to yield 10.00 percent. The notes gained to a 101-7/8 bid after being freed to trade before closing at a 101-1/8 bid.
The paper is rated B1/single-B and Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette was the lead manager.
Iron Mountain Inc's $165 million 10-year notes traded up to 102-5/8 bid on Friday compared with a 102-1/2 bid out of the gate on Thursday.
Flagstar Corp 11-1/4 percent debt due 2004 continued its recovery from two weeks of erosion and ended up two points at 59 bid, 60 offer. The debt rose 3-1/2 points on Thursday.
ValuJet Inc debt was unchanged at 90 bid, 91 offer after rising more than three points on Thursday when the U.S. Department of Transportation approved the airline for operation, one trader said.
Looking ahead to next week's new issue calendar, almost a dozen high-yield deals are lined up to price, plus a few established high-grade names.

Loewen Group, which is embroiled in a hostile takeover bid by Service Corp, has plans to issue $350 million in debt in a two-part private placement deal sometime next week, market sources said. Deal structure is $175 million in five-year and $175 million in seven-year debt.
In the governments market, the 30-year long bond ended off 8/32 at 98-01/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
-- Roanne Daniels, 212-859-1677
